guest.notes: real ipad in a device farm; nothing is emulated here

oss_paths: nvsio/qemu-ios (gpl qemu s5l89xx port: iphone 2g/3g, ipod touch 1g/2g era only)
jprx/darwin-vm (mit, a14-a19: boots a debuggable darwin root shell, no springboard, no apps)
constraints: oss emulation of apple systems does exist and is named in oss_paths, but it is kernel-and-shell grade or ancient-hardware grade: no oss path boots this version with springboard and real apps, which is the whole reason the target exists
apps resolve only through the owner's purchase history for this version, so the device farm stays the only lane that can actually run the abandoned app
firmware and ipsw are apple's and are owner-supplied: we ship none of it, and darwin-vm's own setup script assumes you fetch apple's files yourself
attestation is real on a leased device, which is the one advantage a device farm has over any emulator
no legitimate emulation lane: a physical device, leased one at a time
ipad-only applications are the reason this lane exists: they have no desktop equivalent
the first ipados release, and the home of several abandoned ipad-only tools
